climate.overview_html: The WMO has issued its starkest El Niño warning in the modern observational record: Secretary-General Celeste Saulo described the event as “literally off the monitoring charts,” with Niño 3.4 SST anomalies forecast to reach approximately +3.7–3.8°C above average during the November 2026–January 2027 window — a level that would make this the strongest El Niño in four decades of satellite-era monitoring. Eleven days before the COP31 opening in Antalya (November 9–20), Climate Home News reports that only 77 heads of state or government have confirmed attendance — roughly a third fewer than at the COP28 peak — and raises concerns about civil society access in Türkiye, while Pacific leaders issued the Taku Pakasoa Declaration on emissions, climate finance and ocean protection ahead of the summit. The EU’s adopted negotiating position and a Chatham House briefing frame the talks against the Strait of Hormuz crisis and a widening gap between current policies (2.8°C) and the Paris goal.

items.headline: WMO: Current El Niño May Be “Unprecedented in Strength” — Niño 3.4 Forecast at +3.8°C NDJ 2026–27; SG Saulo Says Event “Literally Off Monitoring Charts” Used Over Past Four Decades
items.summary: WMO's updated seasonal outlook projects that Niño 3.4 SST anomalies may reach approximately +3.8°C above average during November 2026–January 2027, potentially eclipsing the 1997–98 record event. WMO Secretary-General Celeste Saulo said the event is 'literally off the monitoring charts' used over the past four decades. The OND 2026 GSCU already forecast a seasonal mean anomaly of +3.7°C, with warming peaking around December. The WMO Global Seasonal Climate Update projects above-normal surface temperatures across most of the globe for OND 2026, enhanced rainfall over East Africa's October–December rainy season, and a positive IOD expected to peak in October and then decline. The equatorial Atlantic basin is forecast to remain anomalously warm.

items.headline: COP31: Only 77 Heads of State Confirmed for Antalya — A Third Fewer Than COP28; Civic Space Concerns in Türkiye; Campaigners Demand Fossil-Lobby Access Limits
items.summary: With COP31 opening November 9 in Antalya, Climate Home News reports that only 77 heads of state or government have confirmed they will speak at the World Leaders Summit — roughly a third fewer than at the COP28 high-water mark in Dubai. The outlet also highlights civil society concerns about civic space restrictions in Türkiye, where the conference is hosted. Campaigners including Amnesty International are calling for limits on fossil-fuel industry lobbying access at the summit. The reduced head-of-state attendance follows broader diplomatic tensions linked to the Strait of Hormuz crisis and other geopolitical factors running in parallel with the negotiations.

items.headline: Pacific Leaders Issue Taku Pakasoa Declaration Ahead of COP31: Commitments on Emissions, Climate Finance and Ocean Protection; Political Statement Not Yet Binding Negotiating Text
items.summary: Pacific island leaders issued the Taku Pakasoa Declaration ahead of COP31 in Antalya, covering emissions reduction ambition, scaled-up climate finance for adaptation and loss-and-damage, and ocean protection provisions. The declaration represents a unified Pacific political position heading into the November 9–20 summit. The Planet Brief notes it is a political statement rather than settled negotiating text, and the degree to which it influences Antalya outcomes will depend on uptake among developed-country parties. Pacific nations have historically been among the most forceful voices for the 1.5°C temperature limit and for stronger finance commitments from developed countries.

items.headline: EU Adopts COP31 Negotiating Position: Faster Renewables, Energy Efficiency, Fossil-Fuel Transition; EU Parliament Environment Committee Adds Pressure for Greater Ambition on NCQG Finance Goal
items.summary: EU environment ministers formally adopted the EU's negotiating position for COP31 on October 12, 2026. The position calls for accelerated renewable deployment, improved energy efficiency, and stronger language on moving away from fossil fuels, with the launch of the second global stocktake as a central agenda item. The European Parliament's environment committee pressed for greater ambition and faster progress. The EU position also addresses the New Collective Quantified Goal (NCQG) on climate finance, which will be a central negotiating battleground at Antalya. The EU attends COP31 with Australia holding the co-presidency of the conference.

major_events.name: Super Typhoon In-fa (JTWC 30W) — Making Passage Over Northern CNMI Today Oct 30; Typhoon Condition III Active for Agrihan, Pagan & Alamagan; Track Well North of Saipan/Guam
major_events.status: As of Oct 30: RNZ reports the storm regained strength to approximately 150 mph maximum sustained winds as it approached the northern CNMI. Typhoon Warnings are in effect for Agrihan, Pagan and Alamagan; destructive winds are expected throughout Friday, with the core forecast to pass between Pagan and Agrihan around 7 PM local time. Weatherboy confirms the main southern population centres — Saipan, Tinian, Rota and Guam — are well south of the core track, though high surf of 12–18 ft and heavy rainbands will affect the region. NWS Guam projects 6–10 in. of rain and 3–6 ft of coastal inundation for the northern islands. Governor David Apatang has directed residents to shelter from Friday morning through sunrise Saturday. Post-storm damage assessment expected Saturday–Sunday.
major_events.impact: Agrihan/Pagan/Alamagan: Typhoon Warning active; destructive winds (74+ mph) throughout Oct 30; coastal inundation 3–6 ft; 6–10 in. rainfall; shelter in place Fri morning–Sat sunrise. Saipan/Tinian/Rota: heavy rainbands, 12–18 ft dangerous surf, no typhoon condition declared. Guam: outside cone. Main CNMI population centres appear spared direct hit. Damage assessment for remote northern islands expected Sat–Sun.

major_events.name: Southeast Asian Peatland Haze (Indonesia/Borneo/Sumatra) — 120,000+ Satellite Hotspots at 7× 2025 Levels; Indonesia–Singapore Announce Joint Task Force; Wet Season Transition Underway East Kalimantan; Underground Fires Persist
major_events.status: As of Oct 30: The Diplomat reports Indonesia and Singapore have agreed to establish a joint task force to investigate companies allegedly responsible for the transboundary fires, with Indonesia’s foreign minister calling haze a bilateral priority. The Conversation cites satellite analysis showing more than 120,000 fire hotspot detections across Indonesia so far this season — approximately seven times the 2025 full-season total — attributing the scale to exceptional El Niño-linked drought. IQAir data places direct exposure at more than 12.5 million people across seven Indonesian provinces; the heaviest hotspot activity is in Kalimantan and Sumatra, with a secondary front in South Papua. The wet season transition is now underway in East Kalimantan, bringing surface relief, but underground peat burning up to 8 metres below the surface remains active and unresponsive to rainfall or aerial water-bombing. WMO has described the 2026 event as potentially the worst transboundary haze on record in Southeast Asia.
major_events.impact: Indonesia: 333,470+ confirmed acute respiratory cases (7 provinces); ~1.9M ha burned; 120,000+ hotspot detections (7× 2025 total); underground peat fires persist despite surface rain; wet season transition beginning East Kalimantan. Malaysia/Singapore: haze easing but transboundary smoke still detected. Joint Indonesia–Singapore task force announced Oct 30. ~40M people region-wide exposed.

weather.overview_html: Super Typhoon In-fa is passing through the northern CNMI today as the season’s most direct US-territory threat — Typhoon Condition III in effect for Agrihan, Pagan and Alamagan — while tracking well north of the main population centres of Saipan, Tinian, Rota and Guam. The Indonesia–Singapore joint task force announced today marks a diplomatic escalation of the peatland haze response, as satellite hotspot counts running at seven times 2025 levels make this the most severe documented transboundary haze event in Southeast Asia. Elsewhere, NWS Anchorage issued a Storm Warning through October 30 for southwest Alaska, Bristol Bay and the Aleutians — 50-knot winds, gusts to 60 knots, seas to 37 feet. October 2026 enters its final day still on track to set a new warmest-October record in ERA5.

items.source: RNZ / Marianas Variety / Weatherboy / NWS Guam
items.headline: Super Typhoon In-fa Makes Passage Through Northern CNMI on Oct 30: Typhoon Warnings Active for Agrihan/Pagan/Alamagan; 150-mph Sustained Winds; Track Confirmed Well North of Saipan and Guam; 12–18-ft Surf on Main Islands
items.summary: Super Typhoon In-fa made its passage through the Northern Mariana Islands on October 30, with the storm centre tracking between Pagan and Agrihan, the two largest of the uninhabited or sparsely inhabited northern CNMI islands, at approximately 7 PM local time. Typhoon Condition III — destructive winds within 12 hours — was declared for Agrihan, Pagan and Alamagan by Governor David Apatang, directing residents to shelter from Friday morning through Saturday sunrise. Maximum sustained winds near 150 mph were reported by JTWC as the storm approached. The track ran well north of the main population centres of Saipan (population ~48,000), Tinian and Rota, which faced high surf of 12–18 feet and heavy rainbands but not typhoon conditions. Guam was outside the cone. A post-passage damage assessment for the remote northern islands is expected over the weekend; the islands have only a small number of permanent residents.

items.headline: Indonesia–Singapore Announce Joint Task Force on Peatland Haze; Satellite Data Show 120,000+ Hotspots at 7× 2025 Levels; Wet Season Begins East Kalimantan but Underground Fires Persist
items.summary: Indonesia and Singapore agreed October 30 to establish a joint task force to investigate companies allegedly responsible for the 2026 peatland fires, The Diplomat reports, with Indonesia's foreign minister calling haze a top bilateral priority for the two countries. The Conversation cites satellite analysis showing more than 120,000 fire hotspot detections across Indonesia so far — approximately seven times the 2025 full-season total — attributing the severity to El Niño-linked drought extending through the dry season. IQAir places direct haze exposure at more than 12.5 million people across seven Indonesian provinces, with the heaviest hotspot activity in Kalimantan and Sumatra and a secondary front in South Papua. BMKG confirms the wet season transition is now underway in East Kalimantan, but underground peat burning up to 8 metres below the surface cannot be extinguished by surface rainfall or aerial water-bombing and will continue until sustained wet-season rains fully penetrate the peat column.

items.headline: NWS Anchorage Storm Warning: Southwest Alaska, Bristol Bay and Aleutians — ~50-Knot Winds, 60-Knot Gusts, Seas Up to 37 Feet Through Oct 30 Morning
items.summary: NWS Anchorage issued a Storm Warning effective October 29 at 2:25 PM AKDT through October 30 at 5:00 AM AKDT covering southwest Alaska coastal waters, Bristol Bay and the Aleutian Islands out to 100 nm. Forecast conditions include sustained winds around 50 knots with gusts near 60 knots and seas up to 37 feet. Mariners were advised to remain in port. The system is one of several active fall Bering Sea low-pressure events associated with the increasingly active North Pacific storm track during the 2026 El Niño season.

items.headline: October 2026 Enters Final Day on Track for Warmest October on ERA5 Record — ~+0.23°C Above October 2023; Would Be 12th Consecutive Month Above 1.5°C Paris Threshold
items.summary: With October 30 being the penultimate day of October 2026, Copernicus ERA5 tracking and Celsius.earth probabilistic projections confirm the month remains on course to be the warmest October in the modern instrumental record by approximately 0.23°C over October 2023. If confirmed, this would represent the 12th consecutive month globally above the 1.5°C Paris threshold. The persistent warmth is attributed to the reinforcing combination of background anthropogenic warming and the strengthening 2026 El Niño, whose Niño 3.4 SST anomaly set an all-time record high in early October — an intensity now projected to continue intensifying through December.

renewables.overview_html: Two large-scale finance moves headlined the week: Iberdrola priced $1.6 billion in dual-tranche US green bonds on October 27 to fund transmission and US renewable projects, and the European Commission launched the T-MED Investment Platform on October 26 offering up to €4.5 billion in EFSD+ guarantees for Mediterranean renewables, green hydrogen, grids and storage. At the project and equity level, Blackstone closed its Energy Transition Partners V fund at $8.7 billion — 55% larger than its predecessor — and Atmos Renewables completed the acquisition of BayWa r.e.’s Australian portfolio, lifting its combined capacity to over 2 GW across 19 assets.

items.headline: Iberdrola Prices $1.6 Billion Dual-Tranche US Green Bonds — 5.40% 3-Year and 5.85% 7-Year Notes — to Finance US Transmission and Renewable Projects; Closing November 4; Book Demand Exceeded $2 Billion
items.summary: Iberdrola priced $1.6 billion in green bonds in the US market on October 27, returning to the American debt market where its US subsidiaries regularly raise funds. The offering comprised two tranches: $800 million of 3-year notes at a 5.40% fixed coupon maturing November 2029, and $800 million of 7-year notes at 5.85% maturing November 2033. Proceeds will be applied to US electricity transmission infrastructure and renewable energy projects. The deal is expected to close on November 4. Total book demand exceeded $2 billion. Iberdrola's last comparable US green bond issuance was $525 million by NYSEG in August 2024.

items.headline: EU Launches T-MED Investment Platform — Up to €4.5 Billion in EFSD+ Guarantees for Mediterranean Renewables, Green Hydrogen, Grids, Storage and Clean-Tech Manufacturing; Part of €25 Billion Pact for the Mediterranean by 2035
items.summary: The European Commission launched the Trans-Mediterranean Investment Platform (T-MED) in Brussels on October 26, providing up to €4.5 billion in EU guarantee capacity through the European Fund for Sustainable Development Plus (EFSD+) to reduce investment risk and mobilise private capital. The platform targets renewable electricity generation, green hydrogen, cross-border electricity interconnectors, energy storage and clean technology manufacturing in the Mediterranean basin. Commissioner Dubravka Šuica presented it at a Brussels stakeholder event. T-MED sits within the broader Pact for the Mediterranean initiative aimed at mobilising up to €25 billion in total investment by 2035. The June 2026 launch announcement had referenced over €5 billion in guarantee capacity; the October figure of €4.5 billion represents the finalised ceiling.

items.headline: Faria Renewables Acquires 23.1 MW Wind Farm in Boeotia, Greece from EDP Renewables — Deal Finalised October 29
items.summary: Faria Renewables completed the acquisition of a company owning a 23.1 MW wind farm in Boeotia, central Greece, from EDP Renewables on October 29. The transaction is part of EDP Renewables' ongoing portfolio management and asset rotation strategy in Southern Europe. Financial terms were not disclosed. The Boeotia region hosts significant wind resources, and the acquisition expands Faria's footprint in the Greek renewables market.

items.headline: Optivolt Raises $32 Million Series A to Scale Module-Level Solar Power Electronics — VXI Capital Leads; Former SunPower CEO Participates; Manufacturing Expansion Planned
items.summary: Optivolt, a San Francisco startup developing module-integrated power electronics for solar panels, raised $32 million in a Series A round led by VXI Capital, with participation from RA Capital, Valo Ventures, Atlas Innovate and former SunPower CEO Tom Werner. The round brings total funding to $42 million. The company's Power Balancer dynamically redistributes current among solar cell groups in real time, recovering output lost to shading and mismatch, achieving 99.4% conversion efficiency within the power electronics stage itself. Proceeds fund manufacturing expansion. Optivolt was founded by Thiel Fellow Rohit Kalyanpur.

items.headline: Blackstone Closes Energy Transition Partners V at $8.7 Billion — 55% Larger Than Predecessor; Hard Cap Reached; Targets Renewables, Grid, Storage and Clean Industrial Platforms
items.summary: Blackstone announced the $8.7 billion final close of Blackstone Energy Transition Partners V (BETP V) on October 19, reaching its hard cap with significant oversubscription. BETP V is approximately 55% larger than BETP IV ($5.6 billion, closed February 2025). The strategy generally excludes hydrocarbon reserve ownership and extraction, focusing on renewable energy platforms, grid infrastructure, energy storage and clean industrial companies. Early portfolio companies include Kindle, Fisterra and Viridon. Blackstone cites a 34% net IRR since 1997 across its energy transition strategy.

items.headline: Atmos Renewables Acquires ~1 GW BayWa r.e. Australian Portfolio — Two Operating Solar Farms, 262 MW Bullawah Wind Development and Early-Stage Projects; BayWa Refocusing on Core European Markets
items.summary: Atmos Renewables completed the acquisition of BayWa r.e.'s Australian renewables portfolio in mid-October 2026, bringing Atmos's combined portfolio to more than 2 GW across 19 assets. The transaction includes two operating solar farms — Yatpool Solar Park (106 MW, Victoria) and Hughenden Solar Park (20 MW, Queensland) — plus the 262 MW Bullawah Wind Farm development in New South Wales and additional early-stage projects. BayWa r.e. said the divestiture reflects its strategy to focus on core European markets. Baker McKenzie advised BayWa on the sale. No purchase price was disclosed.

science.overview_html: ECMWF’s experimental AIFS-COMPO system — the first global AI model for atmospheric composition, covering aerosols and reactive gases at 10-day lead times in 50 seconds on a single GPU versus ~1,000 seconds on 8,000 CPUs for its physics-based counterpart — represents the week’s most significant operational AI-weather milestone. NPR’s October 26 analysis confirmed Google DeepMind’s model outperformed physics-based counterparts on the track of Hurricane Isaias — but meteorologists note they “can’t explain why” the model succeeds or fails, flagging a critical interpretability gap for operational use. On the climate side, new research in Nature Climate Change projects Southern Africa’s South Indian convergence zone rainfall swings will occur approximately twice as often this century, while a NeurIPS 2026 workshop paper demonstrates that weather foundation models (Aurora 1.5) can rank enhanced rock weathering CO⊂2; removal across unseen fields, pointing toward dramatically cheaper CDR measurement.

items.headline: ECMWF Launches Experimental AIFS-COMPO: First Global AI Atmospheric Composition Forecasting System — 10-Day Aerosol and Reactive-Gas Forecasts in 50 s on One GPU vs. ~1,000 s on 8,000 CPUs for IFS-COMPO
items.summary: ECMWF introduced AIFS-COMPO as an experimental AI-based global atmospheric composition forecasting system, adapting its AIFS weather model to predict aerosols and reactive gases at 10-day lead times. The system covers 187 variables, runs at 3-hourly temporal resolution, and completes a global forecast in approximately 50 seconds on a single GPU — compared to roughly 1,000 seconds on 8,000 CPUs for the operational physics-based IFS-COMPO. Verification against independent atmospheric composition observations shows comparable or improved forecast skill for several key species including aerosol optical depth over the first five forecast days. ECMWF designates IFS-COMPO as its current operational benchmark; AIFS-COMPO remains experimental. The model is trained on CAMS EAC4 reanalysis and operational ECMWF analysis data.

items.headline: NPR: Google DeepMind AI Model Beat Physics-Based Forecasts on Hurricane Isaias Track — Florida Panhandle Landfall Correctly Forecast vs. Louisiana in Physics Models; Intensity Gap and Interpretability Concern Persist
items.summary: NPR's October 26 analysis reports that Google DeepMind's AI weather model outperformed traditional physics-based models on the track forecast for Hurricane Isaias, which made landfall near Destin, Florida as a Category 2 storm in early October. The DeepMind model correctly pointed to a Florida Panhandle landfall while physics-based models indicated a Louisiana track. ECMWF's AIFS and DeepMind's model are described by NHC forecasters as the two AI models with the strongest track performance this season. However, the model trailed the NHC's blended consensus forecast on intensity — a persistent AI gap. Critically, researchers including Brian McNoldy at the University of Miami note they cannot explain why the model makes a given correct or incorrect forecast, a growing interpretability concern for operational use. The NHC currently uses a multi-model consensus approach and provides ongoing feedback to Google DeepMind.

items.headline: China Introduces Two Operational AI Weather Models: Typhoon Cloud Pattern Recognition and 4-Hour Severe Convective Weather Prediction Targeting Precipitation and Thunderstorm Events
items.summary: China's Meteorological Administration unveiled two new operational AI weather models on October 30: one designed to interpret typhoon cloud imagery for storm structure and intensity analysis, and a second focused on predicting severe convective weather — including heavy precipitation and thunderstorm activity — up to four hours in advance. The convective model is intended to support fine-scale local warnings and emergency preparedness for rapidly evolving severe weather events. China Daily reports the models are part of an ongoing national initiative integrating deep learning into operational meteorological services.

items.headline: Nature Climate Change: South Indian Convergence Zone Rainfall Swings to Occur ~Twice as Often This Century — More Intense Rainfall per Event; Major Implications for Southern African Water Security
items.summary: A study published in Nature Climate Change on October 23 reports that climate model projections indicate swings of the South Indian convergence zone — a rainfall-producing circulation feature critical to Southern Africa's water availability — will occur approximately twice as often in the twenty-first century compared with the twentieth century, and will produce more intense rainfall per event. The dual signal of increased frequency and intensity has major implications for water security, flood risk and agricultural planning across Zimbabwe, Mozambique, South Africa and neighbouring countries. The authors note the combined signal complicates planning compared to a simple wetter or drier projection.

items.headline: Nature Geoscience: Delayed Bedrock Uplift Allows Rapid Warming to Trigger Antarctic Ice Sheet Retreat Before Classical Instability Thresholds — Coupled Ice-Sheet / Solid-Earth Model Simulations
items.summary: A study in Nature Geoscience published October 20 uses coupled ice-sheet and solid-Earth model simulations to show that the delay in glacial isostatic adjustment — the slow bedrock uplift following ice mass loss — can allow rapid climate warming to push the Antarctic Ice Sheet into retreat before classical marine ice sheet instability thresholds are reached. The result suggests that traditional stability assessments may underestimate sensitivity to the rate of warming, not just its magnitude, and that the timing of bedrock response relative to ice dynamics is a critical factor in near-term sea-level projections.

items.headline: NeurIPS 2026: Weather Foundation Models for Enhanced Rock Weathering CDR — Aurora-1.5-Based TerraNova-ERW Ranks Removal Across Unseen Fields; Few-Shot Sampling Cuts Measurement Cost 30–90%
items.meta: Munukutla, Oviedo, Zhang, Takeda & Lavista Ferres · NeurIPS 2026 Tackling Climate Change with ML Workshop
items.summary: A paper accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Tackling Climate Change with Machine Learning workshop tests weather foundation models as frozen encoders to predict CO₂ removal rates in enhanced rock weathering (ERW) — a CDR method that spreads crushed silicate rock on agricultural soils. Evaluated with leave-one-field-out methodology across 5,192 chronosequences from 264 fields in Brazil and the US, the best model — TerraNova-ERW, built on Aurora 1.5 — correctly ranks intra-field measurements on fields it has never seen. Zero-shot prediction of a new field's mean removal quantity remains a challenge attributed to data scale limitations. Few-shot prediction with a small number of samples per field does work, and the authors estimate it could reduce sampling requirements on densely measured fields by 30–90%, with significant implications for the cost and scalability of ERW measurement, reporting and verification.

items.headline: npj Climate: Recent Doubling of Global Warming Rate in ERA5 Signals 1.5°C Breach by ~2028 — Jin & Pu Attribute Acceleration to Combined GHG Forcing and Reduced Aerosol Cooling
items.meta: Qinjian Jin & Bing Pu · npj Climate and Atmospheric Science
items.summary: A paper in npj Climate and Atmospheric Science by Qinjian Jin and Bing Pu documents a recent doubling of the global surface warming rate in ERA5 reanalysis data, and argues this acceleration, if sustained, places the crossing of the 1.5°C Paris threshold around 2028. The authors attribute the acceleration to a combination of continued greenhouse gas forcing and reduced aerosol cooling, while acknowledging that the role of internal variability including El Niño in recent record temperatures requires careful attribution. The finding is consistent with growing scientific concern that the 1.5°C threshold will be crossed on a permanent basis this decade.

items.title: Optivolt Raises $32 Million Series A to Scale Smart Solar Panel Power Electronics
items.body_html: Optivolt, a San Francisco startup developing module-level power electronics for solar panels, closed a $32 million Series A led by VXI Capital, with participation from RA Capital, Valo Ventures, Atlas Innovate and former SunPower CEO Tom Werner. The company’s Power Balancer dynamically redistributes current among solar cell groups in real time to recover output lost to shading and mismatch, claiming 99.4% conversion efficiency within the power electronics stage. Proceeds fund manufacturing expansion. Total funding: $42 million. Founded by Thiel Fellow Rohit Kalyanpur.

items.title: Blackstone Closes Energy Transition Partners V at $8.7 Billion — 55% Larger Than Predecessor
items.body_html: Blackstone reached the hard cap on Blackstone Energy Transition Partners V at $8.7 billion, announced October 19, significantly oversubscribed. BETP V is ~55% larger than BETP IV ($5.6 B, February 2025). The strategy excludes hydrocarbon reserve extraction, targeting renewables platforms, grid infrastructure, energy storage and clean industrial companies. Early investments include Kindle, Fisterra and Viridon. Blackstone cites a 34% net IRR since 1997 for the energy transition strategy.

items.title: CarbonFarm Raises €7 Million Series A for AI-Assisted Methane MRV in Rice Cultivation — 19 Countries, 12% of Global Anthropogenic CH₄
items.body_html: Paris-based CarbonFarm closed an oversubscribed €7 million (~$7.8 M) Series A led by Colam Impact to scale its digital MRV platform for rice cultivation across 19 countries. The company combines AI satellite imagery analysis, field-data tools and GHG modelling to estimate field-level methane emissions; rice cultivation represents roughly 12% of global human-caused methane. Proceeds fund project development and certification pipeline in Asia, Africa, Europe and Latin America. Founded 2022.

items.title: Voltus Raises $225 Million Series D to Scale Virtual Power Plant and Demand Response Platform to 20 GW by 2030
items.body_html: Voltus, a San Francisco distributed energy resources company, closed a $225 million Series D led by Generation Investment Management, Activate Capital and Vitol to expand its VPP and demand response platform across North America. Target: 20 GW of aggregated DERs by 2030. First raise since a $31 M Series C in 2021. Vitol’s participation reflects rising investor interest in flexible capacity as AI data-centre demand strains US and Canadian grids.

items.title: Moody’s RMS Launches Australia Cyclone and Flood HD Model — First Unified Framework Covering Wind, Storm Surge, Coastal Flood and Inland Flood with Cyclone Reinsurance Pool Modifiers
items.body_html: Moody’s RMS released the Australia Cyclone and Flood HD Model on its Intelligent Risk Platform — the second peril model in its Australia HD climate suite (after the Bushfire HD Model). The framework covers cyclone wind, cyclone storm-surge coastal flood, cyclone-precipitation inland flood and non-cyclone precipitation inland flood in a single model. It incorporates the Cyclone Reinsurance Pool’s event definition modifiers and a national flood-defence database compiled by Moody’s (Australia has no centralised dataset). Supports Pool reinsurance premium sensitivity testing.

items.title: Enel Green Power North America Finalises 270 MW US Solar Portfolio Acquisition for ~$140 Million Enterprise Value
items.body_html: Enel Green Power North America completed the acquisition of seven operating solar plants with combined capacity of ~270 MW, with an enterprise value of approximately $140 million financed from existing cash flows. Trade press reported the deal around October 9. The plants are fully operational across multiple US states, expanding Enel’s North American renewable portfolio under its Clean Energy Plan.
